lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.27 - A Listen. Then act it out.

details: Listen. Then act it out consolidates the unit language within a narrative context. Students listen to understand the story's plot and humorous twist, then role-play the dialogue to practise fluency and intonation.
Look for attentive listening, understanding of the humorous ending, and confident, expressive delivery of the dialogue when acting out the story.
“Oh no! Minh isn’t feeling well. She’s not at school today. Can you guess what’s the matter? No? Do you want to read and find out? Great!”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down (Listen and Follow): 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (Video, then act it out): 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.27 - B. Choose the correct answers.

details: Choose the correct answers checks students' comprehension of the story. The questions require them to recall key plot details and apply their knowledge of giving good advice to the situation.
Look for accurate selection of the answers for all three questions, showing a clear understanding of the story's events and the appropriate advice.
“That was a funny story about Minh's ten shirts! Let's check if we remember all the details. Read the questions and choose the correct answers to show what you know.”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down:

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.85 - A Read, write, and number.

details: Read, write, and number consolidates narrative comprehension and sequencing skills. Students use context clues to complete the dialogue, then number the story frames in the correct logical order.
Look for the correct words from the word bank written in the blanks, and the correct numbering of the story frames from 1 to 6.

“Oh no, this story about Lien and Jack is all mixed up! Some words are missing and the pictures are in the wrong order. Can you be a story detective, fill in the blanks, and number the pictures to fix it for me?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.28 - C Make your own story.

details: Make your own story encourages creative language use and personalization. Students complete the story template by making choices and filling in their own ideas, then act out their new version to practise speaking fluency.
Look for logically completed sentences in the story based on the students' choices, and confident, enthusiastic role-playing of their unique dialogue.
“I want to write my own story! Can you help me?  Create your own funny story by choosing the words and filling in the blanks. When you're finished, act out your new story for your friends.”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.28 - Tongue Twisters Listen & say

details: Listen and say provides focused pronunciation practice on the vowel sounds ‘oo’ and ‘ew’ (/ʊ/ vs. /uː/). The tongue twister format encourages students to clearly differentiate and articulate the two similar sounds.
Look for clear and accurate articulation of the vowel sounds, with a noticeable difference in pronunciation between words like 'looked' (/ʊ/) and 'flew' (/uː/).
“Let's have some fun with two tricky sounds! The sounds in 'book' and 'flew' are very similar. Listen carefully, then let's try to say these tongue twisters without getting them mixed up!”
